items.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Jo Jones. Roy Eldridge. Dizzy. Charlie Parker.

ctx.x: If you don’t play with Miles. Look at all these people that are in there. They played with Miles. Except Norman Granz’s people, but that’s years ago. Because you know, with Norman Granz, he had Jazz at the Philharmonic, all his people always won the polls. Oscar Paterson. Ray Brown. Jo Jones. Roy Eldridge. Dizzy. Charlie Parker. Illinois Jacquet and Flip Phillips. Who was the trombone player with Woody Herman?

items.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Like, say, the way Papa Jo Jones played vis-a-vis the way Max Roach played... [INTERVIEWEE] Yes, of course.

ctx.x: It’s a harmonic difference between that, and swing is steadier, a steadier rhythm, like the Count Basie mode.
Like, say, the way Papa Jo Jones played vis-a-vis the way Max Roach played with displacements and so on.
